title: Pdf import displaces transparent gradients in pdf created with cairo > 1.11.4
description:
Pdf import displaces transparent gradients in pdf created with cairo > 1.11.4
Migrated from https://bugs.launchpad.net/inkscape/+bug/1078430 (a lot of copy paste but proofread and retested on my current system, did not test across different versions of cairo and their exports)

#### Summary:

- Inkscape incorrectly converts transparent gradients of PDFs to SVG (created by Inkscape export, cairo >= 1.11.4, saving as pdf or printing to pdf via GTK+ print dialog)

#### Steps to reproduce:

- open Inkscape
- open [04831-1.svg](/uploads/b1321b638b765ff1f1ad1454c756e0dd/04831-1.svg) or create a rectangle and give it a gradient (will be `#0000ffff` to `#0000ff00` by default)
- save as pdf (1.4 or 1.5, default values) 
- open created pdf in Inkscape (default internal import)

#### What happened?
- The gradient fills are displaced and partially clipped off
- if poppler/cairo import used, different error occurs (see https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inbox/-/issues/3282).

#### What should have happened?
- The gradient fills in original SVG and opened PDF look identical (or at least very similar)

#### Pdfs affected
##### Affects newer versions of cairo
- problematic pdfs created (by su_v) with cairo 1.12.4, 1.12.6 and 1.12.8 on OS X 10.7.4 (64bit) with GTK+/Quartz builds of Inkscape 0.48.3.1 and Inkscape 0.48+devel r11871.  
- unproblematic pdfs created (by su_v) with cairo (all <= 1.12.2) 1.8.8, 1.8.10 and 1.10.2 on all official Mac OS X Inkscape packages >= 0.47 (in 2012-11-13)
- unproblematic pdfs created (by su_v) with cairo 1.10.2 (X11), 1.11.4 (Quartz) with local builds on Mac OS X 10.5.8 (32bit)
- scaled rsvg-convert pdfs (see doesn't affect section)

<details><summary>pdf rendered in pdf viewers</summary>
Problematic pdf (created with cairo 1.12.8)

- crashed/segfaulted xpdf 3.03 on Ubuntu (does not segfault 3.04-7 on Linux Mint 19.1).  
- rendered with solid fill colors instead of gradient fills on Ghostscript 9.05 on OS X
- rendered normally on Evince 2.30.3 (OS X), 3.6.0 (Ubuntu 12.10), Xpdf 3.02 (OS X), Ghostscript 9.06 (Ubuntu 12.10) and Apple's Preview.app (OS X)
</details>

##### Doesn't affect
- pdfs created with libcairo 1.11.4 or older
    - unproblematic pdfs created (by su_v) with cairo 1.12.2 (X11) with local builds on OS X 10.7.4 (64bit)
    - unproblematic pdfs created (by su_v) with cairo 1.12.2 on a Ubuntu 12.10 x64 VM
- fully opaque gradients, but these imports in a completely different way (transparent gradients are separated into opaque gradient and a mask with a transparency gradient)
- librsvg 2.36.4 (cairo 1.12.8) export (still imported wrong on poppler/cairo import)
    - unless rsvg-convert scales the pdf to match the page size in Inkscape (in which case, internal import has same results). E.g `rsvg-convert --format=pdf --zoom=0.8 --output=04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4-zoom_0.8.pdf 04831-1.svg`, which produced [04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4-zoom_0.8.pdf](/uploads/2f4a9606095007c9db41ecc6bdd6d48c/04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4-zoom_0.8.pdf)

I can confirm that it doesn't affect pdfs exported by the 0.48.5-1 package (7z archive for Windows)

#### Example files
- [04831-1.svg](/uploads/353fe55d4b6cf1507929dda0c8e9abd5/04831-1.svg) -  linked above
- [04831-1-cairo-1_15_10-2ubuntu0_1-838ae0f22d-1_1-dev.pdf](/uploads/b26e9acc45a4167ade98249fb5699db7/04831-1-cairo-1_15_10-2ubuntu0_1-838ae0f22d-1_1-dev.pdf) - Inkscape 1.1-dev (838ae0f22d, 2020-07-14, custom) export, looks slightly different from others
- [04831-1-cairo-from-7z-0_48_5-1_windows.pdf](/uploads/8c846692a369801b1d0aa1961202937b/04831-1-cairo-from-7z-0_48_5-1_windows.pdf) - should be correct, created with 0.48.5-1 r10040 x32 7z archive on Windows 10 x64
- [04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-04831.pdf](/uploads/492db8f0560b6ea735ead24fde9640ee/04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-04831.pdf) - PDF exported with Inkscape 0.48.3.1 and cairo 1.12.8
- [04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-r11871.pdf](/uploads/248bc7b16fdd392eb227de4b2ef7292e/04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-r11871.pdf) - PDF exported with Inkscape 0.48+devel r11871 and cairo 1.12.8
- [04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4.pdf](/uploads/98f129fde2b4b14e48bbd4c13c7109eb/04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4.pdf) - should be imported correctly, but pdf is a different size
- [04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4-zoom_0.8.pdf](/uploads/efb7cc3eddfbf064301c7853a2ff31f3/04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4-zoom_0.8.pdf) - linked above

| older file comparison | comparison on old and new | 
| --- | --- |
| ![1078430-screenshot-comparing-PDF-cairo-versions-in-r11871-osx](/uploads/ca9fd1af9ce7de14b50997dc3b47c26e/1078430-screenshot-comparing-PDF-cairo-versions-in-r11871-osx.png) | ![1078430-screenshot-comparing-old-and-new-exports](/uploads/a2b47f1f61a84485ac960b2ec885e6e8/1078430-screenshot-comparing-old-and-new-exports.png) |

#### Version info from su_v on launchpad
Reproduced on Mac OS X 10.5.8 (32bit), OS X 10.7.4 (64bit) and Ubuntu 12.10 (64bit, VM) with:
- Inkscape stable (0.47-0.48.3.1, various cairo and poppler versions)
- Inkscape trunk r11871 (default PDF input extension) [*]
- Inkscape trunk r11871 (experimental PDF via poppler-cairo input extension)
- PDF -> SVG using pdftocairo (from poppler 0.20.4, 0.20.5)
[*] poppler versions don't seem to affect the result (same import with poppler 0.16.6, 0.16.7, 0.18.4, 0.20.4 and 0.20.5)

#### Version Info (me and others on launchpad)

- Reproduced Inkscape 1.1-dev (838ae0f22d, 2020-07-14, custom) Linux Mint 19.1, libcairo2 1.15.10-2ubuntu0.1
- Reproduced Inkscape 0.92.5 (6c0c36ef5a, 2020-05-15) Linux Mint 19.1, libcairo2 1.15.10-2ubuntu0.1
- Reproduced 0.48.5-1 r10040 x32 7z archive on Windows 10 x64 (though it exported a pdf that did **not** have issues

<details><summary>Some more replication info</summary>
I'm unclear what was tested (is this pdf exports, or imports). If it includes imports, it may conflict against my tests in 0.48.5-1 . Important to know if it conflicts with my tests, so included it

* Reproduced on Windows XP, Inkscape trunk revision 11871, cairo 1.12.8 (local test).
* Not reproduced with cairo 1.11.2.

This is useful, but not too relevant to this report (which focuses on internal import, which corresponds to import with cairo)
Tested with Inkscape 0.91 r13725 on Kubuntu.

Import with cairo:
* 04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-04831.pdf : not displaced but partially clipped off.
* 04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4.pdf : not displaced, not clipped off (correct).
* 04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4-zoom_0.8.pdf : not displaced but partially clipped off.
* 04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-r11871.pdf : not displaced but partially clipped off.

Import with poppler:
* 04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-04831.pdf : not clipped off but displaced and blue gradient not stretched (=circle).
* 04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-r11871.pdf : not clipped off but displaced and blue gradient not stretched (=circle).
* 04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4.pdf : not displaced, not clipped off but blue gradient not stretched (=circle).
* 04831-1-cairo-1_12_8-librsvg-2_36_4-zoom_0.8.pdf : not clipped off but displaced and blue gradient not stretched (=circle).
</details>

title: Theme from Welcome dialog overrides selected theme from preferences
description:
Theme from Welcome dialog overrides selected theme from preferences
#### Summary:
<!-- Summarize the issue/suggestion concisely: -->

The theme set in Welcome dialog overrides the ones chosen from the preferences dialog. Regression from 1.1.x

#### Steps to reproduce:
<!-- Describe what you did (step-by-step) so we can reproduce: -->

- open Inkscape
- From Welcome Screen choose 'Compact' (opens Inkscape with Minwaita+Hicolor-symbolic)
- Choose a different icon-pack (multicolor) from the preferences dialog
- Restart Inkscape

#### What happened?

Inkscape opens with Hicolor icon theme (despite the iconTheme in preferences.xml being multicolor).

#### What should have happened?

Icons/Theme should reflect what was selected.

#### Version info

```
Inkscape 1.2-alpha (07dea3e, 2022-02-18)

    GLib version:     2.64.6
    GTK version:      3.24.20
    glibmm version:   2.64.2
    gtkmm version:    3.24.2
    libxml2 version:  2.9.10
    libxslt version:  1.1.34
    Cairo version:    1.17.4
    Pango version:    1.44.7
    HarfBuzz version: 2.6.4

    OS version:       Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS
```

# Feature Request

## :goal: Goal

As a `shepard frontend user` I want `to see the semantic annotations in the frontend in a highlighted form` so that `I can grasp them easily`.

   1. in a new annotation section of collection
   2. in a new annotation section in data object view
   3. in a annotation column for all types of data references in the data reference content box
   4. in a new annotation section in date reference detail view

title: Allow more customization for pgbouncer
description:
Allow more customization for pgbouncer
### Problem to solve

Currently it is not possible to customize a little bit more pgbouncer deployment, you can only specify the parameters to modify that correspond to `[pgbouncer]` section.

Pooling configuration in SG:

```
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1beta1
kind: SGPoolingConfig
metadata:
  name: poolconfig
spec:
  pgBouncer:
    pgbouncer.ini:
      pool_mode: session
      default_pool_size: '300'
...
```

This generate a configuration file like:

```
$ kubectl exec -it -n gitlab-db gitlab-db-0 -c pgbouncer -- cat /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini
[databases]
 * = port = 5432

[pgbouncer]
listen_port = 6432
unix_socket_dir = /var/run/postgresql
stats_users = postgres
ignore_startup_parameters = extra_float_digits
auth_type = md5
max_db_connections = 0
pool_mode = session
auth_query = SELECT usename, passwd FROM pg_shadow WHERE usename=$1
application_name_add_host = 1
log_disconnections = 1
max_client_conn = 2000
log_stats = 1
log_connections = 1
default_pool_size = 20
max_user_connections = 0
auth_user = authenticator
listen_addr = 127.0.0.1
admin_users = postgres
```

But pgbouncer has three main sections:

1- `[databases]`: To specify database connections.

2- `[users]`: To add some custom configuration for some users

3- `[pgbouncer]` :  To add pgbouncer configurations parameters 


And right now ong the the 3 section is allowed to be modified.

### Further details

In some environments it is required to add some user restrictions like amount of connectios allowed for a user or using different pool mode like : 

```
[users]
user1 = pool_mode=transaction max_user_connections=20
user2 = pool_mode=session max_user_connections=50
```

### Proposal

Add to SGPoolingConfig CRD the options to configure the 3 differents sections:

```
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1beta1
kind: SGPoolingConfig
metadata:
  name: poolconfig
spec:
  pgBouncer:
    pgbouncer.ini:
      databases:  # optional and if not added * = port = 5432 should be the default
        gitlab:

But pgbouncer has three main sections:

1- `[databases]`: To specify database connections.

2- `[users]`: To add some custom configuration for some users

3- `[pgbouncer]` :  To add pgbouncer configurations parameters 


And right now ong the the 3 section is allowed to be modified.

title: Improve Grafana tab on the web console when no pods info is available
description:
Improve Grafana tab on the web console when no pods info is available
Backport to ~"target_version::0.9.6" -> #1086 

--

### Summary

When one cluster has `grafanaEmbeeded` and no pods are available yet, the Grafana tab is shown on the web console even though no data can yet be pulled from it because there are no IPs to match for the pods.


#### Steps to reproduce

- Enter the web console
- Choose a cluster with no pods info available
- Enter the Grafana tab for the specified cluster
- No info is shown and an the following error message can be found on the browser console `Cannot read property 'ip' of undefined`


### Expected Behaviour

If no pod's info is available, provide the user with a message like `No pods yet available`


### Environment

- StackGres version: `0.9.5` / `1.0.0-alpha1`

title: Increase memory limit for prometheus-postgres-exporter container to 256Mi
description:
Increase memory limit for prometheus-postgres-exporter container to 256Mi
We saw that the current minimum size of 64Mi for prometheus-postgres-exporter container memory limit is not enough in some real life usage scenario. The amount of memory measured for such container reached a maximum of 107Mi. We should increase the default memory limit to 256Mi for prometheus-postgres-exporter in order to prevent OOM in more cases. This does not means that users will have to increase it in some edge cases. 

## Implementation plan

Set memory limit to 256Mi for container prometheus-postgres-exporter in class `io.stackgres.common.StackGresContainer`.

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Implement the solution
* [ ] Test the implementation

title: Document how to tweak and upgrade SGDistributedLogs
description:
Document how to tweak and upgrade SGDistributedLogs
Create the following sections under Administration:

* [ ] Document how to tweak an `SGDistributedLogs` by using `stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause` annotation to change the Pod used resources or the Postgres configuration. This section should include a list of specific options a user could touch to avoid break functionality.

Also, the current documentation for upgrading distributed logs is not working since distributed logs database structure changes from `0.9` to `1.0`.

In particular:

* timescaledb extensions version 1.7.4 is not created
* Tables `log_patroni` and `log_postgres` are not timescale hypertables

To make the operation more portable we should create a runbook to:

1. Create a new instance of distributed logs
1. Point the `SGCluster`s to the new distirbtued logs
1. Move all the data from the old instance to the new one with `kubectl exec` + `pg_dumpall` + `psql`-
1. Delete the old distributed logs
